programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Time Of Death: Albert Walker
programmes.d: When a Devonshire fisherman hauled in his nets on July 28 1996, he made a gruesome discovery: among that day’s catch was a dead body. There was nothing to identify the man’s body except a Rolex watch and a small maple leaf tattoo on his hand.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Murder By Mail: Keith Cottingham
programmes.d: In 1984 a parcel bomb was sent to a 53-year-old grandmother living in a tranquil English village. She died of horrific injuries. No one understood why it had happened. The only evidence detectives had was the bomb itself.

James Fairweather was a 15-year-old boy obsessed with serial killers, violent video games and extreme pornography. He stabbed two strangers to death in separate attacks. He was found unanimously guilty by a jury on 22 April 2016.
Sana Muhammad, formerly known as Devi, had left her unhappy arranged marriage to Ramanodge Unmathallegadoo and remarried. She was a pregnant mother of five when he murdered her in her home.
Stephen Port was convicted of the assaults, rapes and murders of Anthony Walgate, Gabriel Kovari, Daniel Whitworth and Jack Taylor. He was sentenced to life imprisonment with a whole life order.

A gangland feud brings years of murder and mayhem into an inner-city community. Journalist Dermot Murnaghan and detective Clive Driscoll delve into the shocking story of Mark Fellows, and the persistence and ingenuity that brought the feud to an end.

Dermot Murnaghan remembers the morning of 2 June 2010 when the news broke of a gunman on the loose in Cumbria, indiscriminately killing strangers. Along with former Met detective Clive Driscoll, Dermot looks back on the remarkable events of that day.

Dermot Murnaghan brings in the homicide expertise of top detective Clive Driscoll to explore the investigation into the death of pharmacist Jessica Patel. Her husband Mitesh claims it’s a burglary gone wrong, but the evidence paints the real story.

In the late 1980s, the community of Sacramento, California, is shaken by the discovery that a serial killer has been living in their midst. Beneath the grandmotherly exterior of Dorothea Puente, a seemingly kind landlady, lurks a chilling secret.

Southern California was gripped by fear as a string of brutal murders left authorities baffled. Patrick Kearney, later dubbed the 'Trash Bag Killer', preyed on young men, luring them with his wicked charm before committing horrific acts of violence.
Phillip Austin, once seen as an ordinary husband and father, shockingly slaughtered his wife, two children, and even the family dogs in an act of unimaginable violence.

In the 1980s, Kansas City was gripped by terror as young men began to vanish without trace. Robert Berdella hid a gruesome secret: his home was a den of torture where his victims were subjected to unimaginable suffering before he murdered them.
The key to solving the toughest homicides lies somewhere within the final 24 hours of the victim's life. This true-crime documentary series follows investigators as they piece together events.
Tai O’Donnell was a talented musician about to make it big - but his ambitions were cruelly cut short after he met a new girl.
Canadian Ashley Wadsworth moved to the UK to be with the long-distance boyfriend she’d met online. Tragically, her family would never see her alive again.

Dawn Walker started looking for love online as her three daughters grew up. Her new partner, Thomas Nutt, quickly moved into the family home - and soon started ripping Dawn’s family apart to ensure Dawn’s world centred around him alone.

Kerry Woolley’s family said she had everything - a loving husband and kids, nice house, smart car and a good job. So when she was gripped by alcoholism, they all rallied round to try and help Kerry get back on her feet.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Clare Wood
programmes.d: In April 2007, Clare Wood met George Appleton on a dating website and they embarked on a relationship together. Unbeknownst to her, Appleton was a criminal with a severe history of violence against women.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Suzy Lamplugh
programmes.d: A look at the case of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh, who showed a client around a house in Fulham in July 1986 and was never seen again. Dermot Murnaghan hosts.
The series returns to take a closer look at the most horrific crimes ever committed on British soil, starting with the May 2017 Manchester Arena bombing.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Ann Maguire
programmes.d: The tragic story of Ann Maguire, who was stabbed to death by a teenage pupil while teaching a Spanish lesson at Corpus Christi Catholic College in Leeds.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Gemma McCluskie
programmes.d: The harrowing story of EastEnders actress Gemma McCluskie, who was murdered by her older brother in the flat they shared in east London in 2012.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Stepping Hill
programmes.d: An inside look at the series of mysterious deaths that occurred at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport, Greater Manchester, in 2011.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Steven Wright
programmes.d: A closer look at the crimes of Steve Wright, who was dubbed 'The Suffolk Strangler' after murdering five women who worked as prostitutes in Ipswich in 2006.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Hitman And The Hairdresser: Fadi Nasri
programmes.d: A 29-year-old hairdresser was found brutally stabbed on her doorstep in a quiet suburban street of London. A recording of a threatening phone call seemed to suggest the motive, but every lead comes to a dead end.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: DNA Of A Murder: Andrew George
programmes.d: Hilda Murrell, a 78-year-old distinguished rose-grower, was found dead in woodland near her home town. Despite a huge investigation by the British police, detectives failed to find her killer and conspiracy theories muddied the waters still further.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Body In The Suitcase: Lorenzo Simon
programmes.d: On 12th May 2014 a human torso was discovered in a suitcase during routine maintenance work on a Birmingham canal. With no useable DNA and no other body parts, the case initially seemed impossible to crack.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Bodies Of Evidence: Roger Severs
programmes.d: In November 1993, Derek and Eileen Severs disappeared without a word. When police spoke to their son, Roger, he insisted they were on holiday. However, there was no evidence of this apparent trip, and Roger was soon arrested on suspicion of murder.
